8	## Step 1: Technology Discovery
9	
10	### 1. ML-Based Bakery Proofing Optimization
11	- **Domain**: Bakery production - dough proofing
12	- **Breakthrough**: Computer vision + humidity/temperature sensor fusion with ML models can now predict optimal proofing endpoints in real-time, replacing manual "poke test" methods. Recent advances in edge-deployable vision models (2024-2025) enable camera-based dough volume estimation at <$200 hardware cost.
13	- **TRL**: 6 (lab-validated, some academic papers; no commercial product specifically for proofing prediction)
14	- **Time to product**: 6-9 months
15	- **Status**: PROMOTED
16	- **Reasoning**: ECD/BakeWatch offers thermal profiling only (no AI, no proofing). Worximity does OEE monitoring but not process-specific proofing optimization. No incumbent addresses the specific proofing prediction problem with ML. Mid-market bakeries (50-500 employee) currently rely on operator experience.
17	
18	### 2. AI Vision for Meat Cutting Yield Optimization
19	- **Domain**: Meat processing - portioning and cutting
20	- **Breakthrough**: 3D vision + AI can map carcass geometry and optimize cutting patterns to maximize yield from each piece. Combines depth cameras with ML models trained on anatomical variation.
21	- **TRL**: 7 (JBT/Marel has high-end systems >$500K)
22	- **Time to product**: 12-18 months
23	- **Status**: REJECTED
24	- **Reasoning**: JBT Marel ($1.7B revenue) dominates this space with integrated hardware+software portioning systems. Scott Automation also competes. The "Robot with a Knife" systems from Marel are already deployed. Competitive density is very high in automated meat portioning. Enterprise-tier market controlled by well-funded incumbents.
25	
26	### 3. Dairy CIP Optimization via Turbidity + Conductivity Sensors + ML
27	- **Domain**: Dairy processing - Clean-in-Place
28	- **Breakthrough**: Combining inline turbidity, conductivity, and flow sensors with ML models to predict CIP cycle endpoint (rather than fixed time cycles). Can reduce water/chemical use 20-40% and increase production uptime.
29	- **TRL**: 6-7 (Ecolab has basic sensor-based 3D TRASAR for water treatment; no AI-specific CIP optimization product for mid-market dairy)
30	- **Time to product**: 8-12 months
31	- **Status**: PROMOTED
32	- **Reasoning**: Ecolab and Diversey offer chemical/service contracts but not standalone AI software. Endress+Hauser sells sensors but no prediction layer. No affordable (<$50K) AI-driven CIP optimization exists for mid-size dairy processors (50-500 employee plants). Current CIP cycles are grossly over-timed, wasting 15-30% water/chemicals.
33	
34	### 4. Cheese Aging Prediction via Multi-Sensor Fusion
35	- **Domain**: Dairy processing - cheese maturation
36	- **Breakthrough**: Combining volatile organic compound (VOC) sensors, humidity/temperature monitoring, and acoustic impedance measurements with ML models to predict cheese ripeness and optimal aging duration.
37	- **TRL**: 5 (still primarily academic; VOC-ML correlation proven in labs but not productized)
38	- **Time to product**: 18-24 months
39	- **Status**: REJECTED
40	- **Reasoning**: TRL too low (5). VOC sensor arrays for cheese aging are still in academic validation. The correlation models between sensor readings and cheese quality are not robust enough across cheese varieties. Time to product exceeds 12-month threshold. Capital requirements for sensor development would be high.
41	
42	### 5. Distillery Spirit Aging Prediction via Micro-Oxygenation Monitoring
43	- **Domain**: Spirits production - barrel aging
44	- **Breakthrough**: Inline dissolved oxygen sensors + temperature/humidity tracking combined with ML models trained on aged spirit chemical profiles (GC-MS data) to predict aging trajectory and optimal extraction timing.
45	- **TRL**: 5-6 (academic papers demonstrate feasibility; no commercial product)
46	- **Time to product**: 12-18 months
47	- **Status**: REJECTED
48	- **Reasoning**: TRL borderline. The spirits aging market is conservative and dominated by tradition. Craft distilleries (the mid-market) are small operations with limited tech budgets. The addressable market for AI aging prediction is small - most craft distillers produce <10,000 cases/year. ROI case is weak because aging is a cost of goods, not a controllable loss.
49	
50	### 6. Bakery Ingredient Ratio Optimization via ML
51	- **Domain**: Bakery production - recipe/formulation
52	- **Breakthrough**: ML models trained on production data (ingredient supplier variability, ambient conditions, dough rheology) to dynamically adjust ingredient ratios for consistent product quality. Leverages recent advances in small-data ML and flour/ingredient characterization.
53	- **TRL**: 6-7 (KPM Analytics Mixolab provides rheological data; ML layer on top is feasible)
54	- **Time to product**: 6-9 months
55	- **Status**: PROMOTED
56	- **Reasoning**: KPM sells Mixolab hardware ($30-50K) but no AI prediction layer. Aptean provides ERP but not process-level ingredient optimization. No product exists that takes flour quality variability data and recommends real-time recipe adjustments for mid-market bakeries. Flour quality varies significantly between batches, causing waste.
57	
58	### 7. Meat Trim Reduction via 3D Scanning + Pattern Optimization
59	- **Domain**: Meat processing - trimming waste reduction
60	- **Breakthrough**: Low-cost 3D structured-light scanning of primal cuts before trimming, combined with ML to generate optimal trim paths that minimize waste while meeting specification.
61	- **TRL**: 7 (vision-guided trimming exists in high-end systems)
62	- **Time to product**: 12 months
63	- **Status**: REJECTED
64	- **Reasoning**: Same competitive landscape as #2. JBT/Marel's Innova system and integrated portioning lines already do this at scale. The problem is that the hardware (automated trimming robots) is the hard part, not the software. Software-only trim optimization without robotic execution has limited value because human trimmers cannot follow complex ML-generated paths consistently. Competitive density: 4+.
65	
66	### 8. Craft Brewery Fermentation Prediction via Sensor-ML Platform
67	- **Domain**: Brewing - fermentation process control
68	- **Breakthrough**: Low-cost IoT sensors (dissolved O2, pH, specific gravity, temperature) combined with ML models that predict fermentation endpoint, off-flavor risk, and optimal dry-hop timing.
69	- **TRL**: 7 (Precision Fermentation/SENNOS already has basic monitoring; ML prediction layer is the new value)
70	- **Time to product**: 6-9 months
71	- **Status**: REJECTED
72	- **Reasoning**: Precision Fermentation (now SENNOS) already offers BrewIQ with IoT sensors + cloud monitoring for breweries. BeerSmith and Brewfather provide recipe-level optimization. The market is crowded: SENNOS, BrewMonitor, Plaato, and others offer IoT fermentation monitoring. Competitive density: 4-5. Adding an ML prediction layer is incremental, not a new product.
73	
74	### 9. Bakery Oven Energy Optimization via Thermal Modeling + ML
75	- **Domain**: Bakery production - oven energy efficiency
76	- **Breakthrough**: Combining thermal imaging of oven chambers with ML models that predict optimal heating profiles (zone-by-zone) to minimize energy use while maintaining product quality. Industrial ovens consume 40-60% of bakery energy.
77	- **TRL**: 6 (thermal profiling exists via ECD; AI optimization layer does not)
78	- **Time to product**: 8-12 months
79	- **Status**: PROMOTED
80	- **Reasoning**: ECD provides thermal profiling hardware (M.O.L.E. sensors) but explicitly has NO AI/ML capabilities. They measure; they do not optimize. No competitor offers ML-based oven energy optimization specifically for bakeries. With energy costs rising 30-50% since 2022, mid-market bakeries are desperate for energy savings. The technology leverages commodity sensors + ML software.
81	
82	### 10. Dairy Heat Exchanger Fouling Prediction
83	- **Domain**: Dairy processing - heat treatment
84	- **Breakthrough**: Inline pressure differential and temperature sensors combined with ML models to predict heat exchanger fouling progression and optimal cleaning timing. Reduces unplanned downtime and over-cleaning.
85	- **TRL**: 6-7 (pressure/temp sensors are commodity; ML prediction of fouling curves is proven in academic literature but not productized for mid-market)
86	- **Time to product**: 6-9 months
87	- **Status**: PROMOTED
88	- **Reasoning**: Endress+Hauser and IFM sell sensors but no prediction software. Ecolab sells chemicals but not predictive fouling models. AVEVA/OSIsoft PI system is enterprise-grade ($200K+) and not dairy-specific. No affordable (<$50K) fouling prediction product exists for mid-size dairy processors. Fouling causes 5-15% production loss in dairy plants. This is a pure software play on commodity sensors.
